correctness.rationale: Invariance of first and second lifted momentum moments gives E[kick]=0 and 0=2E[p kick]+E[kick^2], and Cauchy–Schwarz gives the inequality. On the positive-variance equality locus the Cauchy equality coefficient is -1/2, so p-m=-kick/2, P-m=kick/2; invariance gives sin Theta=-sin theta. Consequently the second iterate has p2=p and theta2=theta+2m. Iterating sin(theta+2m)=sin theta shows either sin m=0 or cos(theta+m)=cos(theta+3m)=0; the latter with sin m nonzero forces m=pi/2 modulo pi and then sin theta=0, contradicting positive kick variance. Thus m belongs pi Z and T^2=id on the invariant full-measure set. Ergodicity then restricts support to one two-cycle. Direct exact orbit arithmetic verifies K=2pi: (pi/2,-pi) ↔ (3pi/2,pi), with Var(p)=pi^2 and Var(kick)=4pi^2. The saved verify.py algebra was inspected, but is not used as a proof of the trig branch.
residual_risks: Unbounded momentum invariant measures without second moments fall outside the assumptions; finite test alone does not prove the sine resonance step.

value.rationale: The exact orbit-rigidity equality case turns a routine second-moment balance into a dynamical diagnostic: all compact stationary states satisfy a sharp measurable variance bound, and a positive-kick ergodic saturator is necessarily a two-cycle. Both the nontrivial dynamical obstruction and explicit sharp orbit distinguish the contribution from textbook covariance algebra. Natural use in standard-map invariant-measure analysis, no claim about chaotic ergodicity.
residual_risks: Value resides in the standard-map equality classification, not in the generic stationary-increment identity.

final_claim: On the Chirikov cylinder map with K nonzero, every compact invariant measure has E[sin theta]=0 and Cov(p,K sin theta)=-Var(K sin theta)/2, hence Var(p)>=Var(kick)/4; equality with positive kick variance forces mean p in pi Z and T^2=id almost surely, with ergodic equality exactly on nontrivial two-cycles and an explicit attaining K=2pi orbit.
limitations: Compact support on real-lifted p, not torus momentum or diffusive unbounded trajectories; no claims about existence/uniqueness/absolute continuity of chaotic invariant measures.
Other-map covariance sources and primary standard-map literature do not exhaust all possible unindexed prior work.
